children: By Junko Fujita

Japan's Nikkei share average erased early gains to end little changed on Tuesday, as higher oil prices and rising bond yields hurt investor sentiment, while SoftBank Group rebounded from a selloff in the previous session.
The Nikkei
closed 0.01% lower at 63,484.1 after rising about 1% earlier. The broader Topix
"The rise in oil prices as well as higher government bond yields weighed on investor sentiment," said Daisuke Hashizume, senior strategist at Daiwa Securities.
"Today's trade was led by short-term investors and they sold stocks for profits from gains earlier in the session."

Oil prices rose nearly 2% as concerns over supply disruptions lingered after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline and cast doubt on efforts to ease shipping risks in the Gulf.
Japan's government bond yields rose, with the 10-year yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) hitting its highest since September 1996.
Shares of chip-related firms Advantest
and Tokyo Electron
gave up early gains to fall 2.96% and 0.55%, respectively.
SoftBank

jumped 7.54%, recovering part of the previous session's 10.7% slide after a selloff in AI-linked stocks triggered by warnings from industry leaders about the technology's risks. Memory chip maker Kioxia
rose 2.29%.
"Japan was the first market that was hit by the warning from the AI leaders in the previous session," said Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities.
"The morning after, investors thought it was too early to judge the fate of the pace of AI investments by hyperscalers."
Banks fell, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group
and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group
down 1.4% and 2.67%, respectively.
Sony Group
fell 1.66%.
Of the more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 51% rose, 44% fell and 4% traded flat.
